landmarks.name: Helsinki Cathedral
landmarks.writeup: A distinctive white neoclassical cathedral located in the capital, symbolizing Finnish Lutheran heritage.

wiki.extract: Helsinki Cathedral is the Finnish Evangelical Lutheran cathedral of the Diocese of Helsinki, located in the neighborhood of Kruununhaka in the centre of Helsinki, Finland, at the Senate Square. The church was originally built from 1830 to 1852 as a tribute to the Grand Duke of Finland, Emperor Nicholas I of Russia. It was also known as St Nicholas's Church until Finland declared its full independence in 1917. It is a major landmark of the city, and one of the most famous historical structures in Finland as a whole when viewed globally.

landmarks.name: Suomenlinna
landmarks.writeup: An 18th-century sea fortress spread across six islands, recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage site.

wiki.extract: Suomenlinna, or Sveaborg, is a sea fortress composed of eight islands, of which six have been fortified. Located about four kilometres (2.5 mi) southeast of the city center of Helsinki, Finland, Suomenlinna is a popular destination for both tourists and locals, who enjoy it as a picturesque picnic site.

landmarks.name: Santa Claus Village
landmarks.writeup: Located in Rovaniemi, it is known as the official hometown of Santa Claus and a popular tourist destination.

wiki.extract: Santa Claus Village is an amusement park in Rovaniemi, a city in the Lapland region of Finland. It was opened in 1985.

landmarks.name: Olavinlinna Castle
landmarks.writeup: A 15th-century medieval castle in Savonlinna, famous for its annual opera festival.

wiki.extract:
Olavinlinna, also known as St. Olaf's Castle, is a 15th-century three-tower castle located in Savonlinna, Finland. It is built on an island in the Kyrönsalmi strait that connects the lakes Haukivesi and Pihlajavesi. It is the northernmost medieval stone fortress still standing and also the best preserved of all the medieval castles in the Swedish realm.
The castle forms a spectacular stage for the Savonlinna Opera Festival, which was held for the first time in the summer of 1912.

landmarks.name: Northern Lights (Aurora Borealis)
landmarks.writeup: A natural light display visible in Lapland, attracting visitors for its spectacular night sky phenomena.

wiki.extract: An aurora is a natural light display in Earth's upper atmosphere caused by charged particles from the Sun colliding with atoms in the atmosphere. These collisions excite oxygen and nitrogen, which then emit light of different colors such as green, red, and purple. When observed in high-latitude regions they are called polar lights and aurora polaris. In the Arctic they are called the northern lights or aurora borealis; in the Antarctic, the term southern lights or aurora australis is used. Auroras display dynamic patterns of radiant light that appear as curtains, rays, spirals or dynamic flickers covering the entire sky.

cultural_events.name: Vappu
cultural_events.writeup: A spring festival celebrated on May 1st, marking workers' day and student festivities with picnics and parties.

wiki.extract: Walpurgis Night, an abbreviation of Saint Walpurgis Night, also known as Saint Walpurga's Eve and Walpurgisnacht, is the eve of the Christian feast day of Saint Walpurga, an 8th-century abbess in Francia, and is celebrated on the night of 30 April and the day of 1 May. This feast commemorates the canonization of Saint Walpurga and the movement of her relics to Eichstätt, both of which occurred on 1 May 870.

cultural_events.name: Juhannus (Midsummer)
cultural_events.writeup: A midsummer celebration involving bonfires, sauna, and gatherings to mark the longest day of the year.

wiki.extract: Midsummer or Midsommar is a celebration of the season of summer, taking place on or near the date of the summer solstice in the Northern Hemisphere, the longest day of the year. The name midsummer mainly refers to summer solstice festivals of European origin. These cultures traditionally regard it as the middle of summer, with the season beginning on May Day. Although the summer solstice falls on 20, 21 or 22 June in the Northern Hemisphere, it was traditionally reckoned to fall on 23–24 June in much of Europe. These dates were Christianized as Saint John's Eve and Saint John's Day. It is usually celebrated with outdoor gatherings that include bonfires, maypole dancing and feasting.

cultural_events.name: Helsinki Festival
cultural_events.writeup: An annual arts festival featuring music, theater, and dance performances across Helsinki.

wiki.extract: The Helsinki Festival is the largest multi-arts festival in Finland. It is Finland's biggest cultural event in terms of visitors. In 2015, around 295,000 people visited the Helsinki Festival.

cultural_events.name: Savonlinna Opera Festival
cultural_events.writeup: A prestigious summer opera festival held in the medieval Olavinlinna Castle.

wiki.extract: Savonlinna Opera Festival is held annually in the city of Savonlinna in Finland. The Festival takes place at the medieval Olavinlinna, built in 1475. The castle is located amid spectacular lake scenery.

cultural_events.name: Kaamos Festival
cultural_events.writeup: A winter festival in Lapland celebrating the polar night with music and cultural events.

wiki.extract: Repugnant was a Swedish death/thrash band from Stockholm active from 1998 to 2004. The band has been cited as one of the first revivalists of the Swedish death metal movement, along with Kaamos. They recorded their only studio album Epitome of Darkness in 2002, but it was left unreleased when the band broke up in 2004, only being published in 2006. Vocalist and guitarist Mary Goore recruited a new lineup of Repugnant to perform at the Hell's Pleasure festival in 2010, as well as several other shows, ending at the Maryland Deathfest in the United States on 29 May 2011. Following the break up of Repugnant, Forge went on to form and front the Swedish rock band Ghost, where he achieved a higher level of success and fame.

food_writeup: Finnish cuisine emphasizes fresh, seasonal ingredients such as fish, rye bread, berries, and mushrooms. Traditional dishes include karjalanpiirakka (rice pies), kalakukko (fish pie), and reindeer meat, reflecting the country's Nordic heritage.
brief_history: Finland was part of Sweden until 1809, then became an autonomous Grand Duchy under Russia. It declared independence in 1917. The country experienced a civil war in 1918 and remained neutral during World War II. Post-war, Finland developed a strong welfare state and joined the European Union in 1995.
current_conflicts: Finland is not involved in any active military conflicts. It maintains a policy of military non-alignment but has recently joined NATO as of 2023.
